module.purpose: Provides shared interpolation logic for transitioning between tldraw draw-shape segment collections.
module.summary: This module decodes vector paths from two collections of draw segments, normalizes their point counts by repeating each collection's final point, interpolates coordinates and optional depth values according to progress, and re-encodes the result as one freehand segment. It is a synchronous geometry utility used by shape interpolation workflows.
module.businessContext: Supports smooth visual transitions for freehand drawing shapes in the tldraw editor. Failure can produce malformed or discontinuous shape animations.
functions: interpolateSegments (~L4-49): Interpolates decoded points into one freehand segment.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Two segments with matching point counts are interpolated at the requested progress.
given: startSegments = [{ type: 'free', path: encodePoints([{ x: 0, y: 0 }]) }]
endSegments = [{ type: 'free', path: encodePoints([{ x: 10, y: 20 }]) }]
moduleContractTests.then: The returned segment contains a point with x equal to 5 and y equal to 10.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Guards linear interpolation of point coordinates.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The start and end segments contain different numbers of points.
given: startSegments = [{ type: 'free', path: encodePoints([{ x: 0, y: 0 }]) }]
endSegments = [{ type: 'free', path: encodePoints([{ x: 10, y: 10 }, { x: 20, y: 20 }]) }]
moduleContractTests.then: The returned segment contains two points and the missing start point is the final available start point.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins the contract for equalizing point-list lengths by repeating the final point.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Interpolation is performed over one or more input segments.
given: startSegments = [{ type: 'free', path: encodePoints([{ x: 0, y: 0 }]) }]
endSegments = [{ type: 'free', path: encodePoints([{ x: 1, y: 1 }]) }]
moduleContractTests.then: The result is an array containing exactly one segment whose type is 'free'.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Guards the output representation independently of the number of input segments.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Interpolated points do not provide z coordinates.
given: startSegments = [{ type: 'free', path: encodePoints([{ x: 0, y: 0 }]) }]
endSegments = [{ type: 'free', path: encodePoints([{ x: 10, y: 10 }]) }]
moduleContractTests.then: The returned point has z equal to 0.5.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins the default depth value when either endpoint lacks z.

detail.name: interpolateSegments
preconditions: Each segment path must be decodable by b64Vecs.decodePoints using its dimension metadata.
When either input produces points, both inputs must produce at least one point for interpolation to have defined behavior.
postconditions: Returns an array containing exactly one segment.
The returned path encodes one interpolated point for each position up to the longer decoded point array length.
Each output point contains x, y, and z coordinates.
invariants: All input segments are flattened into a single point sequence before interpolation.
If one decoded point sequence is shorter, its final point is reused for missing positions.
When both corresponding points have defined z values, z is linearly interpolated; otherwise output z is 0.5.
edgeCases: Both inputs contain no decoded points: returns one free segment whose path encodes an empty point array.
Inputs contain different numbers of decoded points: the shorter sequence is extended by repeating its final point.
Exactly one input contains no decoded points while the other contains points: interpolation attempts to access a missing point and throws a runtime TypeError.
Malformed or undecodable segment paths: errors from point decoding propagate because the function does not catch them.
Progress values outside the usual 0-to-1 range are passed directly to lerp without clamping.

raises: Runtime TypeError when one side has no decoded points and the other side has at least one point
Errors raised by b64Vecs.decodePoints or b64Vecs.encodePoints
errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No explicit validation or recovery is performed; runtime and dependency errors propagate.

detail.summary: Interpolates the decoded points from two collections of draw-shape segments at the specified progress and returns them as one freehand segment.

specLiterals.role: Fallback z coordinate when either corresponding point lacks a defined z value.

specTests.then: It returns exactly one segment of type 'free'; each coordinate is the linear midpoint of the corresponding start and end coordinates.
The final start point is reused for every missing start position, and the result still contains one output point per position in the longer sequence.
It returns one free segment encoding an empty point sequence.
